issue_context.title: Consider adding support for `TryParse` as a way to bind primitives
comments:
Thanks for contacting us.

We're moving this issue to the `.NET 7 Planning` milestone for future evaluation / consideration. We would like to keep this around to collect more feedback, which can help us with prioritizing this work. We will re-evaluate this issue, during our next planning meeting(s). 
If we later determine, that the issue has no community involvement, or it's very rare and low-impact issue, we will close it - so that the team can focus on more important and high impact issues.
To learn more about what to expect next and how this issue will be handled you can read more about our triage process [here](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/docs/TriageProcess.md).

* I wouldn't make `ParameterBindingMethodCache` public. 
* You could introduce a `TryParseModelBinder` instead that is registered to run after `SimpleTypeModelBinder`. Users can remove it if they're don't want it (thus avoiding the need for a option type).

> * I wouldn't make `ParameterBindingMethodCache` public.

I have the same opinion, but I prefer to capture the possibility here for discussion if we should rewrite or reuse. I saw that was decided rewrite most of the code for minimal and probably the same will happen here.

> * You could introduce a `TryParseModelBinder` instead that is registered to run after `SimpleTypeModelBinder`. Users can remove it if they're don't want it (thus avoiding the need for a option type).

I think introduce the `TryParseModelBinder` is a good idea, and probably the user will not need to remove it most of the time. However, the point to use the option is to allow/or not the new behavior when setting the `IsComplexType` property. that affects how the parameter is inferred.

An alternative option is creating a new internal property to the `ModelMetadata`, maybe `HasTryParse`, that will be set when the TryPare method is detected, and we can condition the `TryParseModelBinder` execution to that, however, even in this situation to infer the parameter from `Path` or `Query`, instead of `Body`, I fell we would need to add a new option, to the `APIBehaviorOptions` instead, to allow users to roll back to the previous behavior.

review_comments: Suggestion - we could update `FindTryParseMethod` to not throw via an additional parameter. Not catching exceptions is certainly a lot nicer since it avoids things like first-chance exceptions in VS.
Agree. I will open a new PR just for that, ok?

A future/alternative implementation would look like:

```suggestion
internal sealed class TryParseModelBinder<T> : IModelBinder where T : IParseable<T>
```

Similar to the Array and collection model binder, this would be generic and we would use MakeGenericType to create the correct impl.

@davidfowl  That is an interesting approach, but I don't see the `IParseable<T>` been implemented all around yet. Can we rely on it already?  Or it is just something to think about in the near future?
I have updated the ModelBinder to be generic but without the type constraint for now.
That's fine, I wonder if you need to compile an expression tree at all in the MVC case. Lets chat about this.

This seems wrong, if you can't find a TryParse method then the next binder should be called. Or probably more accurately, the TryParseModelBinderProvider shouldn't create a Binder if no TryParse method is found.

That is exactly what the TryParseModelBinderProvider does and will move to the next provider https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/01c0dd6deac58fdc66f2b06c708c89f332b4ef4b/src/Mvc/Mvc.Core/src/ModelBinding/Binders/TryParseModelBinderProvider.cs#L22

However, we are not creating but still possible to an instance of the binder be created anywhere else, so, I added this additional check.  As alternative option I could change the binder constructor to receive the `Expression Func` in addition to the type, so, in this case the binder is only created with a TryParse available. Is that make sense?

IsParseableType is not set based on availability of a TryParse method though.
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/40233/files#diff-8d5c9542ae556c3865f0ab1ef77402ce730dde4931d5d73f048eecebd23873bfR350

Ah, I missed this:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/40233/files#diff-6d3bdd92c82f5fd4e02279697a8883ea8ed50228d7b7abdde158c1c88dc3d0b8R89-R92
The variable names all started looking the same :D

Exactly! Do you think we should change the names to something else? Any suggestions to make it clearer?

Since we will have an option, I tried to avoid the `IsParseableType` in the `BindingMetadata` class but maybe it is a little bit confusing.
Honestly I would remove null checks for internal types when the inputs are devised by us. That's what the compiler's nullability enforcement is for

I can do that, however, we decided to keep this Binder internal instead of public as the other Binders are. I wonder if, in the future, we will decide to make it public and we will miss this null check.
Add a comment here with the shape of the generated code. It really helps when debugging.
Should the format exception use https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/Mvc/Mvc.Abstractions/src/ModelBinding/Metadata/ModelBindingMessageProvider.cs#L41-L47 as the message?

That is exactly what the TryAddModelError will do: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/c9628273f5e37a9a07b174960ff2228de8b7d4dc/src/Mvc/Mvc.Abstractions/src/ModelBinding/ModelStateDictionary.cs#L290
Hmm, this might be a behavior change. If it previously called the overload that did not supply a culture, it would have defaulted to `CurrentCulture`.

I don't think it does. The `ParameterBindingMethodCache` was previously using `Expression.Constant(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)` when the parameter is available.

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ce292b36cfcbf2d8488b1ea235eae1949fb0c8bc/src/Shared/ParameterBindingMethodCache.cs#L114
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ce292b36cfcbf2d8488b1ea235eae1949fb0c8bc/src/Shared/ParameterBindingMethodCache.cs#L125
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ce292b36cfcbf2d8488b1ea235eae1949fb0c8bc/src/Shared/ParameterBindingMethodCache.cs#L136

With my change, we will keep doing exactly the same (only using it the when the parameter is available) however the `Expression` will come from the caller.

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/50dfb9d622eadec5b6751ba4bb928116a8ca1f3a/src/Shared/ParameterBindingMethodCache.cs#L114
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/50dfb9d622eadec5b6751ba4bb928116a8ca1f3a/src/Shared/ParameterBindingMethodCache.cs#L125
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/50dfb9d622eadec5b6751ba4bb928116a8ca1f3a/src/Shared/ParameterBindingMethodCache.cs#L136

For all the other scenarios the `Culture` expression will be ignored. Eg.:

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/50dfb9d622eadec5b6751ba4bb928116a8ca1f3a/src/Shared/ParameterBindingMethodCache.cs#L67
What is a little bit confusing is the `tryParseMethodCall` is a `Func` that return the `Expression` to be used, not the actual call to the `TryParse` method.
Can we just create a delegate from a func and cache it instead of creating an expression tree?
Yep and the generic helps in that case
In theory you could get away simply having a generic method. Either way, since the expression tree doesn't go all the way up like RDFactory, it seems like more work to have it.
Let me work on it and I will update the PR as soon I have something.
